name: LAB Dessert & Coffee
notes: Own site (macaronsandcoffeelab.com) and its /menu, /dessert pages list items with no prices anywhere in the HTML. SinglePlatform (places.singleplatform.com/lab-dessert--coffee/menu) has a priced Coffee+Sandwich menu but is missing Cakes/Macarons entirely (a core category for this dessert shop) and its coffee prices run 15-80% below DoorDash's, plus it never mentions the 'Zumbar Coffee Beans' branding DoorDash's descriptions use -- treated as stale per playbook guidance on SinglePlatform. DoorDash's server-rendered JSON-LD (schema.org Menu) gives a complete 8-section, 82-item menu (Cakes, Classic/Specialty Espresso Drinks, Ice Blended, Smoothies, Tea & more, Sparkling Ade, French Macarons) with no uniform markup divisor (odd-cent POS-style pricing, not a clean 1.1/1.2x pattern), so used as medium confidence. Uber Eats storefront (also linked from the restaurant's own site) 403'd to WebFetch and was not reachable without a browser.

name: Phra Ram 9
notes: Own site (pr9thai.com) is a single-page Squarespace site with no menu page and no prices anywhere. Ordering is via a ChowNow storefront (direct.chownow.com/order/2274 and /order/40335) which is a client-side app with no server-rendered menu -- needs a browser. DoorDash's server-rendered JSON-LD (schema.org Menu) gave a full 11-section, 91-item catalog; address in the JSON-LD Restaurant block (3705 Avocado Boulevard, La Mesa, CA) matches the work list exactly. Dropped the 'Most Ordered' carousel (12 items) entirely -- every item in it was a verbatim name+price duplicate of an item already in a real category (Pad Thai, Spring Roll, curries, etc.), unlike some carousels that hide unique items. Also deduped 'Salmon Fried Rice' which was listed under both Specialties and Noodles and Rice at the same $22.00 price. Prices are round-dollar with no markup divisor pattern, but DoorDash is a delivery marketplace rather than the restaurant's own platform, so kept at medium confidence.
